guideTitle: 6 Best Trash Cans for Apartments in 2026
metaDescription: Six apartment trash cans compared by footprint, capacity and lid noise, from a 3.1 gallon hang-in-cabinet bin to 13 gallon step cans for small galley kitchens.
introParagraphs: Apartment kitchens ask more of a trash can than a house does. The floor is small, the cabinet under the sink is usually full, the walls are thin enough that a slamming lid carries to the neighbors, and the nearest dumpster or chute may be a walk away. A good apartment can is compact, quiet, easy to carry and clear about what bag it takes.

The six cans here cover the range. The Glad Roomate is a 12 liter bin that hangs inside a cabinet door, the N. NETDOT is a 2.6 gallon three-pack, the simplehuman is a 10.6 gallon slim step can with a slide lock, and the MOVECOM, SONGMICS and KdbK are 13-gallon step cans measuring up to about 24 inches tall. They split into small-footprint and full-size options, so you can choose by floor space.

We evaluated each from its listing specs and the themes buyers raise most, looking at footprint, noise, bag fit and how easy each is to take out. The sections below sort the picks by kitchen size, so you can match one to your galley, studio or one-bedroom layout.

products.name: simplehuman 40 Liter Slim Kitchen Step Can with Slide Lock
specs: Slide lock for pets and children
products.description:
The simplehuman is the one pick built for the squeeze of a small kitchen. It holds 40 liters, or 10.6 gallons, in a slim, space-saving shape, and the plastic body is lighter to move than steel. Built-in wheels make it easy to roll out from its corner when you need to clean around it, an underrated detail in a small apartment where you wipe the floor often.

The lid uses patented technology for a slow, silent close, which means no slam echoing through a shared wall at night, and it can stay open for as long as you like during longer chores. A slide lock holds the lid shut to keep pets and curious children out of the trash, handy if you rent with a dog or cat. The listing does not specify exact dimensions, so measure the gap before you buy.

It is smaller than the 13-gallon MOVECOM, SONGMICS and KdbK, so it fills sooner and suits one to three people. In return you get wheels, a lock and a slimmer profile than those three. Against the Glad Roomate, it stands on the floor rather than hanging in a cabinet. If floor area is the scarcest resource in your apartment, the simplehuman is the best balance of size and features.
products.bestFor: Small galley kitchens with a pet or a toddler.

products.name: MOVECOM 13.2 Gallon Step-On Kitchen Trash Can
products.description:
The MOVECOM is the most carefully specified full-size can here. It measures 13.78 by 15.16 inches and 24.02 inches tall when closed, opening to 33.86 inches, and the listing says it fits under standard 36 inch island counters. For an apartment with a breakfast bar, that single number is helpful.

The interior is bucketless, which maximizes capacity: the listing says it holds up to 40 water bottles of 16.9 ounces or 80 cans of 12 ounces. An integrated liner rim hides bag edges, a rear carry handle makes it easier to move to the door, and non-slip rubber feet keep it steady on tile, hardwood or low-pile carpet. The ABS body wipes clean, and the lid has a stainless-steel overlay.

The pedal is rated for more than 150,000 presses and the one-piece ABS hinge is described as tested beyond 300,000 open and close cycles. The lid opens to about 80 degrees, to avoid counter bumps, and stays open at about 95. Compared with the simplehuman it holds more but is not slim, and compared with the SONGMICS it uses plastic, which is lighter. For an apartment with a counter overhang to respect, the MOVECOM is the safest full-size choice.
products.bestFor: Kitchens with an island or breakfast bar overhang.
cons: Takes more floor than the simplehuman

products.name: SONGMICS 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Pedal Trash Can
products.description:
The SONGMICS is the can to buy when the kitchen is small but you still want it to look intentional. The fluted design adds a decorative touch, and the listing describes a shimmering stainless surface with a metallic-enhanced powder coating that resists rust, oxidation and wear. In a studio, where the can is visible from the living area, that looks like a design choice rather than a utility bin.

It works with a step pedal or by lifting the lid manually to 90 degrees to keep it open during longer tasks, and the lid closes slowly and quietly. The detachable inner bucket allows mess-free emptying and easy liner changes, and 15 matching trash bags in code K come in the box, so you can use it right away. The listing does not give pedal ratings or dimensions, so measure carefully.

It is an ordinary 13-gallon capacity, similar to the MOVECOM and KdbK, and a good deal larger than the 10.6 gallon simplehuman. Against the KdbK, the SONGMICS adds the fluted styling and a named bag code, while the KdbK adds a quoted 200,000-use pedal figure. For a studio or open plan apartment where appearance counts, it is the most attractive option.
products.bestFor: Studio or open-plan apartments where the can is on view.
cons: No pedal rating on the listing

products.name: KdbK 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Pedal Trash Can
products.description:
The KdbK is a straightforward steel step can that skips the frills. The brushed stainless body is described as anti-fingerprint, the handle and base are ABS with an anti-slip design, and the listing says 20 trash bags sized for a 13-gallon can are included. For someone moving into a new apartment and buying everything at once, a can that ships with bags is one less shopping errand.

The lid uses a bi-force damper that pulls it shut slowly, with an anti-slamming design to avoid pinching hands, and it can stand up at 90 degrees for kitchen chores. The inner bucket is ABS, described as strong against impacts, and a small hole lets you fix the bag in place. The pedal is quoted as tested 200,000 times, with a service life over 25 years, which is a maker claim.

Of the three 13-gallon cans, the KdbK is the plainest and offers the clearest pedal durability number. The MOVECOM gives you counter-height dimensions and the SONGMICS gives you styling. Next to the simplehuman, the KdbK is larger and heavier, but it holds more per bag and needs fewer trips down the hall. For a family of two or three in a one-bedroom, it is a reliable default.
products.bestFor: New renters who want a can and bags in one box.
pros: Hole holds the bag in place

products.badge: Best for Small Spaces Without Floor Room
products.name: Glad Roomate 12 Liter Under Counter Waste Bin
specs: Dual lid: flip back or slide front
products.description:
The Glad Roomate is for apartments with almost no floor room. It measures 7 by 9.5 inches and 17.1 inches tall, holds 12 liters (3.1 gallons), and hangs on the inside of a cabinet door with a sturdy over-the-door hook. A strong adhesive hanger lets you set the height, and the listing stresses no drilling or screws, which is the right thing to say to anyone worried about a security deposit.

The lid has two modes: flip back for quick access, or slide front to keep it open during cleanup. It can also stand on its own as a regular can, or be hung outside a cabinet, and the listing mentions using it to collect compost scraps or serve as a bedside bin. The slim size is aimed at counters, bathrooms, laundry rooms and offices, but it is explicitly a small bin, so the listing asks you to measure your space.

With only 3.1 gallons, it is not a primary kitchen can for a household that cooks daily. It makes sense as a prep bin for peels and packaging, paired with a larger can, or as the only bin for a single person. Next to the NETDOT three-pack at 2.6 gallons each, it has a more flexible mount. For a cabinet-first approach, nothing else here comes close.
products.bestFor: Renters who want a bin off the floor with no drilling.

products.name: N. NETDOT 2.6 Gallon Slim Trash Can with Lid, 3-Pack
products.description:
The NETDOT three-pack suits apartments where trash is a bathroom, bedroom and kitchen issue rather than one big bin. Each can holds 2.6 gallons, or 10 liters, in a slim ABS body, and the listing says the profile fits narrow areas such as bathrooms, bedrooms and small kitchens. The lid is described as a secure barrier to keep curious pets from rummaging.

The maker says the lid traps smells and the smooth surfaces are easy to keep clean, which fits well with apartments where the cans sit close to living areas. ABS is described as durable and resistant to wear. Three cans mean you can place one in each wet room and keep a spare for the entryway or office.

It is a supplement, not a main kitchen can. At 2.6 gallons each, compared with the 13 gallons of the KdbK or MOVECOM, a family of three would fill these quickly. Against the Glad Roomate, the NETDOT sits on the floor and does not need a cabinet door. If you want a main kitchen can plus bathroom and bedroom bins, pair the three-pack with a larger step can like the KdbK.
products.bestFor: Small apartments with trash needs in several rooms.
cons: Too small for a main kitchen can

buyingCriteria.explanation: In an apartment, inches decide everything. The MOVECOM is 13.78 by 15.16 inches and 24.02 inches tall, opening to 33.86 inches, which the listing says fits under a 36 inch island counter. The Glad Roomate is only 7 by 9.5 inches, and the simplehuman is a slim step can. Measure the floor space, the counter overhang and the pedal clearance before you buy, then add room for the open lid.

A slamming lid echoes in a small apartment and travels through thin walls. The simplehuman is built for a slow, silent close, the SONGMICS closes slowly and quietly, and the KdbK uses a bi-force damper that avoids slamming. A plain lid like the NETDOT's can click. If you cook late or come home at night, a soft-close lid is a courtesy to your neighbors and your own sleep.

Apartment dwellers often walk their trash to a chute or dumpster, so how often you fill a bag matters. Thirteen-gallon cans like the KdbK, MOVECOM and SONGMICS fit standard kitchen bags and need fewer trips. The simplehuman at 10.6 gallons suits one to three people, and the Glad Roomate at 3.1 gallons is a prep bin. If the walk is long, favor the larger can.

Some cans reduce the first-week errands. The KdbK includes 20 bags and the SONGMICS includes 15 in code K, so you can use them as soon as you unpack. The MOVECOM has an integrated liner rim to hide bag edges. Check bag size on each listing so you do not buy the wrong size, and decide whether you want a can that uses standard supermarket bags.

Rentals limit what you can screw into a wall. The Glad Roomate hangs with an over-the-door hook and a strong adhesive hanger, with no drilling or screws, according to the listing. Floor-standing cans such as the MOVECOM use non-slip rubber feet so they stay put on tile, hardwood or low-pile carpet. A can that does not need installation is easier to take with you when you move.

In a small space, a pet or toddler is never far from the trash. The simplehuman has a slide lock that holds the lid shut, the NETDOT lid is described as keeping pets out, and the Glad Roomate tucks inside a cabinet. Open or loose-lid cans are easier to raid. If you have a curious dog or cat, a lock or a cabinet is more reliable than a heavier lid.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed dimensions and shapes, from the Glad Roomate at 7 by 9.5 inches to the MOVECOM at 13.78 by 15.16 inches. We also noted where a listing gives a counter-height figure, like the MOVECOM's fit under a 36 inch island, because that kind of detail saves a buyer from ordering something that will not fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and lid behaviour
howWeEvaluated.description: Because apartments share walls, we looked closely at lids. The simplehuman's silent close, the SONGMICS's quiet slow close and the KdbK's anti-slamming damper were credited. We noted which lids stay open, such as the MOVECOM at about 95 degrees and the KdbK at 90, and which are simple covers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and trash runs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacities from 2.6 gallons on each NETDOT up to 13.2 gallons on the MOVECOM, and thought about how often a typical one to four person household would walk a bag to the chute. Larger cans scored better for families, and smaller bins scored well as secondary or prep bins.

howWeEvaluated.title: Renter practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered what a renter needs: no drilling, easy moves and bags that are simple to buy. The Glad Roomate's adhesive hanger, the MOVECOM's rubber feet and the KdbK and SONGMICS starter bags all counted. Anything that needs a permanent install was treated as a drawback for apartments.

howWeEvaluated.title: Durability claims
howWeEvaluated.description: Where a listing gave durability figures, such as the KdbK's pedal tested 200,000 times or the MOVECOM's pedal rated beyond 150,000 presses, we noted them as maker claims. Cans without a stated figure, like the SONGMICS, were judged on materials and finish instead, since a rating is not the only way to judge build quality.

faq.q: What size trash can is best for an apartment?
faq.a: For one to three people, a 10 to 13 gallon can is usually enough, such as the simplehuman at 10.6 gallons or the 13-gallon KdbK. A couple who cooks often may prefer 13 gallons to cut down on trips. A hanging bin like the Glad Roomate works as a prep bin beside a larger can.

faq.q: Can I use a small hanging bin as my main trash can?
faq.a: Only for a single person with light cooking. The Glad Roomate holds 3.1 gallons, which fills in a day or two for most households. It shines as a prep and scrap bin or in a bathroom, and it frees your floor for a larger can elsewhere.

faq.q: Which can is quietest for thin walls?
faq.a: The simplehuman is designed for a slow, silent close, and the SONGMICS and KdbK also describe quiet, slow closing lids. A plain-lid can like the NETDOT can click shut. Placing any pedal can on a mat also helps cut floor noise.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about my deposit?
faq.a: Floor-standing cans cause no damage, though rubber feet like the MOVECOM's help avoid scuffs on hardwood. The Glad Roomate hangs on a door hook and an adhesive hanger with no drilling, according to its listing. Test the adhesive on an inconspicuous area and follow the removal advice when you move.

faq.q: How do I keep an apartment trash can from smelling?
faq.a: Take the bag out before food waste sits for days, close the lid fully and wipe the rim every week. A lid that seals, like the NETDOT's, helps traps smells. If you have a trash chute, keep a small scrap bin and empty it often.

faq.q: Is stainless steel worth it in a rental?
faq.a: Steel looks neat and wipes clean, but it adds weight and is not required. The MOVECOM's ABS body is lighter, which helps when you carry it to the dumpster or move apartments. Choose steel such as the KdbK or SONGMICS for appearance or the plastic simplehuman for easy handling.

faq.q: Do I need a can with a lock?
faq.a: Only if pets or small children are around. The simplehuman has a slide lock that holds the lid shut, and the NETDOT lid is described as keeping pets out. Otherwise a heavy lid and a corner placement may be enough, although a hanging bin inside a cabinet avoids the problem.
